content: This unit was introduced by James D. Hardy, Herbert G. Wolff, and Helen Goodell, researchers at Cornell University, based on their investigations into the nature of pain conducted during the 1940s and 1950s. They defined one dol as equivalent to a just noticeable difference (jnd) in the perception of pain, representing the smallest increment of pain that a person could reliably detect. Despite its scientific basis, the dol did not achieve widespread adoption in clinical or research settings. Modern pain assessment now relies on alternative methods that are more commonly accepted and utilized in both medical practice and research.
